origin.description: Upper Lorenz bound of Mehran for data that are reported only as class means and class frequencies.
origin.details: For data reported only as class means and class counts, the ordinary Lorenz curve from Lc is the lower envelope, the one with no inequality inside a class. Lc.mehran fills in the upper envelope consistent with those same class totals.
origin.value: An object of class "Lc" with components p and L only.
origin.example:
# income distribution of the USA in 1968 (in 10 classes)
# x vector of class means, n vector of class frequencies
x <- c(541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261)
n <- c(482, 825, 722, 690, 661, 760, 745, 2140, 1911, 1024)

# compute minimal Lorenz curve (= no inequality in each group)
Lc.min <- Lc(x, n=n)
# compute maximal Lorenz curve (limits of Mehran)
Lc.max <- Lc.mehran(x,n)
# plot both Lorenz curves in one plot
plot(Lc.min)
lines(Lc.max, col=4)

# add the theoretic Lorenz curve of a Lognormal-distribution with variance 0.78
lines(Lc.lognorm, parameter=0.78)
# add the theoretic Lorenz curve of a Dagum-distribution
lines(Lc.dagum, parameter=c(3.4,2.6))

translation.description: Upper Lorenz bound of Mehran for data that are reported only as class means and class frequencies.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Class frequencies, the same length as x.

translation.details: The lower curve is Lc with the same class means and counts. The upper curve follows Mehran's construction: successive slopes are chosen between the chord slopes of the lower curve and the slopes of the reflected polygon, points with a non-finite population share are dropped, and the result is returned with the Lorenz ordinates only.
translation.value: A dict with NumPy arrays p and L.
